title: Unit Circle Definition
text: $$\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)$$ represents the y-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{3\pi}{4}.$$\n##figure4.gif##

title: Reference Angle
text: The reference angle for $$\frac{3\pi}{4}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{4}.$$ The absolute values of the coordinates are given by the legs of a $$45-45-90$$ triangle with hypotenuse $$1$$. The x-coordinate and y-coordinate lengths are equal and satisfy the Pythagorean theorem: $$1=\sqrt{x**2+x**2}=\sqrt{2}x,$$ so both coordinates are $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$$\n##figure5.gif##

title: Quadrant Sign
text: The angle $$\frac{3\pi}{4}$$ is in the second quadrant, where y-coordinates are positive. Therefore, $$\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.$$\n##figure6.gif##
